$comment: Verbatim, read-only cua-driver 0.28.2 outputs captured on the machine described below, with the redaction noted in `redaction`. No input was injected, no pixels were read, no host setting was changed: every argv below is a probe, an inventory, or a deliberately invalid invocation that the driver refuses. Consumed by core/tests/workstation-live.test.ts.

invocation.args: JSON on STDIN, never in argv

recordedRefusals.$comment: Verbatim refusal payloads from the prior read-only probe session recorded in docs/architecture/KAI_WORKSTATION.md section 2. NOT re-run by this capture: reproducing either one means invoking `click`, and this capture injects no input. Both calls were chosen precisely because they cannot deliver input — a pid that does not exist, and a fabricated snapshot handle the driver fails closed on. Both exited 0.

refusal.message: element_token is stale; call get_window_state again to refresh

redaction.$comment: The two window inventories are the driver's REAL output with one field removed: every `title` is replaced by REDACTED_TITLE, and the accessibility tree's process list is replaced by its count (`processes_redacted`). Those fields describe what the OPERATOR was doing on their own desktop and are not load-bearing for this contract — the tests assert window ids, geometry, `app_name` and counts, never a title's text. Everything else (pids, window ids, bounds, z_index, layer, is_on_screen, minimized, app_name, and every other probe in this file) is verbatim.

list-tools.stdout:
bring_to_front: Activate `pid`'s window (or `window_id` if specified) -- bring it to the OS foreground
browser_click: Click a page element (by ref) or viewport coordinates in an exactly-bound tab
browser_dialog: Inspect or resolve a page-owned JavaScript alert, confirm, prompt, or beforeunload dialog on one exactly-bound tab
browser_download: Trigger one download through an exact live browser ref and save it inside an explicitly approved directory
browser_navigate: Navigate one tab of an exactly-bound browser target to a new URL (http/https/about only)
browser_pointer: Perform hover, right-click, double-click, scroll, or drag in an exactly-bound browser tab
browser_prepare: Explicitly prepare an owned DevTools endpoint for a browser
browser_set_input_files: Assign one or more explicit absolute local files to an exact live <input type=file> ref through CDP
browser_type: Type text into an exactly-bound tab via the Input domain
check_for_update: Check the saved stable/nightly Cua Driver channel for a release on GitHub
check_permissions: Check required permissions for cua-driver-rs on Windows
click: Left-click against a target pid
clipboard_read: List available system clipboard types and optionally return privacy-sensitive plain text
clipboard_write: Replace the system clipboard with exactly one value: plain text, an image from an absolute local path, or a file URL from an absolute local path
debug_window_info: Diagnostic: dump everything cua-driver sees about a pid's top-level windows from the daemon's session perspective
double_click: Double-click against a target pid
drag: Press-drag-release gesture from (from_x, from_y) to (to_x, to_y) in window-local screenshot pixels
end_session: End one visible lifecycle session and run its cursor, recording, configuration, and other cleanup hooks exactly once
escalate_session: Deprecated compatibility tool for legacy capture-scope sessions
get_accessibility_tree: Return a lightweight snapshot of the desktop: running processes and on-screen visible windows with their bounds and owner pid
get_agent_cursor_state: Return the session cursor's theme, semantic playback, position, visibility, and motion
get_browser_state: Read-only browser inspection
get_config: Report the current persistent driver config
get_cursor_position: Return the current mouse cursor position in screen points (origin top-left)
get_desktop_state: Capture the full display in true screen pixels with no downscale
get_recording_state: Report the current trajectory recorder state: whether recording is enabled, the output directory (when enabled), and the 1-based counter for the next turn folder that will be written
get_screen_size: Return the size of the main display in physical pixels plus its display scale factor
get_session: Read content-free lifecycle, cursor, recording, and idle status for one session visible to this authenticated transport
get_session_state: Deprecated compatibility alias that reads a live legacy session's capture policy
get_window_state: Walk a running app's UIA tree and return BOTH a structured `elements` array (preferred) AND a Markdown rendering of the same tree (back-compat)
health_report: Single-call end-to-end driver diagnostics
hotkey: Press a combination of keys simultaneously — e.g
install_ffmpeg: Install the ffmpeg binary used by start_recording's video capture (Linux/Windows; macOS records natively and needs no ffmpeg)
invoke_menu: Resolve an exact application-menu path one live native level at a time and invoke its final item through accessibility APIs
kill_app: Force-terminate a process by pid
launch_app: Launch a Windows app hidden — the driver never brings the target to the foreground, the target's window is launched with SW_SHOWNOACTIVATE so it does not steal focus from whatever is currently frontmost
list_apps: List Windows apps — both currently running and installed-but-not-running — with per-app state flags:
list_sessions: List content-free lifecycle summaries attached to this authenticated transport lease
list_windows: List every top-level window currently known to the window manager
move_cursor: Move the agent cursor overlay to (x, y)
page: Legacy browser compatibility tool
press_key: Press and release a single key, delivered directly to the target pid's top-level window via PostMessage(WM_KEYDOWN/WM_KEYUP)
replay_trajectory: Replay a recorded trajectory by re-invoking every turn's tool call in lexical order
right_click: Right-click against a target pid
scroll: Scroll the target pid's focused region
set_agent_cursor_enabled: Show or hide the agent cursor owned by a session
set_agent_cursor_motion: Configure only movement physics and visibility timing for a session cursor
set_agent_cursor_theme: Select an already-installed cursor theme for a session
set_config: Write a setting into the persistent driver config
set_value: Set a value on a UIA element via the ValuePattern interface
set_window_frame: Set one exact top-level window's frame in the desktop-coordinate space reported by list_windows and verify the resulting geometry through an independent readback
start_recording: Start trajectory recording
start_session: Optionally create or return a lifecycle session before acting
stop_recording: Stop trajectory recording
type_text: Insert text into the target pid via character-by-character PostMessage(WM_CHAR) to the focused window
verify_state: Deterministically verify bounded predicates against one exact window
zoom: Zoom into a rectangular region of a window screenshot at full (native) resolution

err-argv-json.stderr:
error: positional JSON arg to 'cua-driver call' did not parse: expected ident at line 1 column 2
       received: not-json

hint: PowerShell 5.1 strips quotes around JSON field names in
      multi-field args. Pipe the JSON via stdin instead:
        '{"pid":1234,"window_id":5678}' | cua-driver call get_screen_size

      Or use PowerShell 7+ (pwsh) which preserves the quotes.
